data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2024 Sweden note summarizes questionnaire-based results for lower secondary teachers and principals collected in 2024. It reports percentages for teachers’ background (age, gender, non-teaching experience), perceptions and practices related to teaching for today’s world (e.g., adapting to cultural diversity, special education needs, social and emotional learning), technology use (including AI use), and teachers’ learning opportunities (initial teacher education, induction/mentoring, continuous professional learning). It also covers teacher leadership/autonomy, professional relationships (with colleagues, principals, students, and parents/guardians), status of the profession, employment terms, sources of stress, classroom management/student behaviour, and professional outcomes (lesson aim fulfilment, well-being, job satisfaction, and intention to leave). The note explicitly comments only on statistically significant differences or changes relative to the OECD average and flags that some estimates may be affected by non-response bias. No student-level predictive modelling or plausible-value scaling is involved; the document is intended for policy interpretation of descriptive patterns rather than causal inference.
